Good questions.

A little more
under the hood.

Does the agent ever see the secret?+

The normal run flow passes the secret to the approved command’s environment, not to the agent. grantd replaces exact matches of injected values in stdout and stderr before returning that output.

This is exact-match redaction: encoded or transformed values can get through. Always review the command you’re approving.

Do I approve every command?+

You can approve one run, allow matching requests for a limited time, or create a standing grant. Grants are scoped to a caller label, project directory, secret names, and command prefix. Matching requests can then run without a new prompt; every use is still audited.

Creating a grant requires approval. Keep its scope narrow and its lifetime short.

Which agents can I use it with?+

grantd has an MCP server and a command-line interface. Claude Code has a dedicated connection flow in the app. Other coding agents, including Codex and Cursor, can integrate through MCP or call the CLI.

Does grantd make any command safe?+

No. An approved command receives the secret and can send it elsewhere. grantd does not sandbox commands or restrict network access, and it cannot protect a compromised user account.

The important boundary is your approval of the command and any grants you create.

Which platforms does it support?+

The current app is for macOS 14 and later. It includes a menu-bar app, a local background service, a CLI, and an MCP server. Touch ID is used for approval, with macOS account-password fallback when needed.

Is it open source?+

Yes. grantd is licensed under Apache 2.0. It runs locally, with no cloud account or sync service required.
